gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the battery runtimes it quoted are Eco-mode figures that come with a dimmer picture. The XGIMI Vibe One, sold as the battery pick under $300, switches itself to Eco on battery: ProjectorCentral measured 64 lumens there against 229 plugged in, for a rated 1.2 hours. XGIMI's own MoGo 4 page says its 2.5 hours is Eco-only and you get less time if you leave Eco.
standout_why: I compared against The Hook Up's 'Read BEFORE You Buy a Portable Projector in 2026' (cited). It covers the general trade-off between brightness and runtime, but only for the TCL PlayCube, Aurzen Zip Pro and NexiGo. It also covers powering the Elfin Flip Plus from a power bank through a 20 V USB-C-to-barrel converter. It says nothing about battery-mode brightness on the MoGo 4, Capsule 3 or Vibe One. The two RTINGS lists ChatGPT cited (under-500 and portable) loaded with no article body through my fetch, so I could not check them line by line. ChatGPT's own answer gives 'up to 2.5 hours' for the MoGo 4 and Capsule 3 without saying it's Eco mode, and sells the Vibe One on its 'built-in battery'.
decides: For a shopper who answers 'Yes' to ChatGPT's 'Do you need a built-in battery?', this rules out the Vibe One. On battery it falls back to Eco by default at about 64 measured lumens, rated for 1.2 hours, so it's for a dark room or the outlet only. The MoGo 4 holds up better as the battery pick: 71.28 Wh, and it plays through USB-C PD from a power bank of 65 to 150 W. But the 2.5-hour figure is for Eco, and Expert Reviews measured 1 h 52 min in Standard. The Capsule 3 is also rated 2.5 h only in Eco, and its brightest setting is 200 ANSI lumens. Of the plug-in picks, the MoGo 2 Pro is the only one XGIMI says can run from a power bank over 65 W. The Elfin Flip Plus has only a DC IN port, so off the wall it needs a converter (per The Hook Up). That makes a Dealectric USB-C power bank of 65 W or more a fitting add-on for the MoGo 2 Pro and MoGo 4.
